purpose: last untested construction: can removing market exposure leave something behind?

beta_decomposition_strategy_vs_universe.reading: 59% of variance is idiosyncratic, but the alpha is not statistically significant at |t|>2

rolling_beta_hedge_to_zero.note: rolling beta estimator produced unstable sizing and a pathological drawdown; treated as an implementation artefact, not evidence

hedged_results.interpretation: the stable fixed hedge is the fair test. At a 0.2 hedge ratio Sharpe is flat at 1.144 versus 1.130 unhedged, i.e. inside noise, while return halves. Removing beta removes return and buys no improvement in risk-adjusted quality. There is no isolated alpha to harvest.

conclusion: every construction has now been ruled out: long/short, trend, mean reversion, volatility breakout, intraday, reversal, cross-sectional momentum, beta-hedged momentum. The cross-sectional momentum signal is statistically real (IC +0.0174, t=2.93) but its risk-adjusted quality (Sharpe 1.13) is below simply holding the universe (Sharpe 1.30), and hedging it away does not reveal hidden alpha. It is a lower-drawdown implementation of beta, not a source of excess return.
